elections.quote: Another week, another Dem primary where the polls, prediction markets, and talking heads got it wrong. Given that this happened just a week ago in MI, one would think we might have learned. Hong could still win in WI, but the certainty in the outcome in this race was misplaced.
Fwiw, it looks like about 80% of the precincts in Madison have reported already, so Hong is going to need to find more votes somewhere else.
I'm not from Michigan, so the fact that there is no such place as South Detroit doesn't bother me, but this is a good ad.

The average polling error in MI looks to be double digits. Some thoughts on this:

- I hope those pollsters share some introspection as to how they missed so badly. 

- A lot of very smart people on this site acted like this race was decided a week ago.

- I never again want to see reporting on prediction markets as if they are a useful tool for gauging where races stand. They're easily manipulated and are going to magnify any polling error. It's crazy that credible news outlets rely on them as such.

- We need to win this Senate race. If AES does pull this out, an important immediate question is if he underperformed his primary polling so badly, will he do the same in the general election tests in those same polls? I don't think so, but it's an important question.

Still a lot of votes to be counted in Michigan (I'm not staying up for it), but it seems likely that the flood of late polls showing El-Sayed winning by a strong double digit margin are going to be pretty far off.

I don't know who's going to win this race (I just know that we need to help them win in Nov) but the idea that any pollster would have a client down 14 pts in a primary poll and tell them "there's no path to victory" is silly. Primary polls are far less reliable due to turnout.
Waiting another minute to get out of this race is wildly irresponsible. He is owed nothing by anyone and needs to get out of the way.
If the options are truly either we have to listen to you lie about voter fraud or let you pass a voter suppression bill, then fine - keep on lying.

Good news for Dems - the Dem margin has been steadily improving among all groups since Trump took office. And this is the first time, outside of pre-election bumps, that the Dem downward turn among Black voters has reversed.  And Dems have even improved substantially with whites.

This election happened in August of last year, in a district that Trump carried by 11 pts in 2024. The Dem candidate, Catelin Drey, won by an almost identical margin, representing an almost 22 pt swing towards Dems, resulting in GOPs losing their supermajority in the IA Senate.
Let's keep in mind, the GOP reportedly spent upwards of $80 million on their primaries in Texas, well more than double the amount spent by Dems.
Here are 4 districts the TX GOP gerrymandered to gain seats in November, with the Dem and GOP primary vote. Dems outvoted GOPs in every one of them.

Wow, the Dem primary turnout among Hispanic voters in Texas is going to be giving the GOP sweats for the next 8 months. 

Take Zapata County - turnout in the Dem primary there yesterday was 143% the total number of votes Harris won in the 2024 general election. That's wild.
For those claiming fraud because Spencer Pratt did worse as the later ballots were counted, this chart is of the registered Dem share advantage over registered GOPs by each day of ballot returns.
